page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v5 is an EDSv5-family virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The underlying hardware features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 8 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Each core supports hyper-threading with 2.0 threads per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. This instance includes a 614 GB local storage disk and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the E16ds_v5 consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. The single-core stress-ng performance is recorded at 1905.99, while multi-core performance reaches 15490.01. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 837.18 GB/sec, which drops to 52.98 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 38.57 GB/sec. In database and key-value store operations, the server achieves 15.92 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a PassMark database score of 7992.24. Notably, the server demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models (135M parameters) at 289.27 tokens per second, though larger 7B models run at an average speed of 12.36 tokens per second.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU and a dedicated 614 GB local disk, the E16ds_v5 offers balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated hardware. The inclusion of local storage and Premium Storage capability makes it highly suitable for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate data processing tasks. The lack of GPU resources and average multi-core scaling limits its suitability for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI training, but it remains a solid, cost-efficient choice for enterprise applications, web serving, and software compilation.
